messages:
incident-bot: Pager - HIGH: Horizon Financial (tenant:horizon-prod) experiencing sustained 503s and model degrade since 1777777600. Impact: customer facing LLM responses failing or low-quality due to fallback to tiny-safe variant. Escalation: on-call.
cs-horizon: We're seeing errors on their VPC-dedicated pool. Customer reports timeouts and then responses that are short and incorrect. They say this started after autoscaling spike around 1777777400.
alex: looking. I can see increased error rate on their tenant routing table -> many requests hit fallback chain to redwood-small-safe. Latency also spiking. Pinning history shows a recent auto-fallback policy triggered.
maria: can you paste the routing policy id? I want to check if fallback is default for this tenant.
alex: policy id: rb-policyr-0453. Fallback target: redwood-small-safe (quantized). Error logs show KV-cache misses and OOM-ish signs on some nodes: "evicting-kv-cache: true" across 3 GPUs.
jess (sre-lead): paging eng-runtime. This looks like degradation not full outage. Customer impact: degraded quality and 15-20% 5xx. We should avoid a full disable of fallback (might increase 5xx). Proposal: short-term pin to a safe-medium model (redwood-3b-safe-v1) for horizon-prod with a canary ramp, and create explicit carve-out to skip autoscale fallback only for their tenant until we stabilize.
tom (eng-runtime): I can push a tenant-level override. Command I'll run (w/ audit):

```
redwoodctl override set --tenant horizon-prod --model redwood-3b-safe-v1 --pin 2h --reason "mitigate degraded fallback during VPC pool instability"
redwoodctl routing update --tenant horizon-prod --disable-auto-fallback --duration 2h
```
alex: I recommend also adding a graceful fallback policy that prefers regional replica before falling to tiny-safe. That reduces quality regression.
beth (sales): heads-up: I'm on the call with Horizon CS in 10m. If we pin, can we guarantee no PII exposure or change to logs? Need to confirm for them.
leo (oncall): I'm taking initial oncall handoff. Alex, once tom runs override, I'll validate traffic split and monitor SLOs. Maria, can you prepare selector that routes 5% to redwood-3b-safe-v1 first? We'll ramp to 50% over 20 minutes if error rate stays <2%.
maria: will do. Ramp plan: 5% -> 20% (10m) -> 50% (10m) with rollback conditions: 5xx > 3% or p50 latency > 1200ms.
cs-horizon: please also include a customer-facing note I can send to Horizon support inbox explaining we're pinning to a higher-capacity safe variant temporarily and engineering is investigating root cause.
alex: capturing traces for affected requests: trace ids 0001-0007 (sample). Also I've opened infra ticket INF-8712 to check node mem pressure. Looks like GC spikes when KV cache warms.
tom (eng-runtime): override applied.
incident-bot: Action logged: override.set by tom (eng-runtime) @ 1777777922. Audit id: A-99821.
leo (oncall): can confirm initial canary at 5% is live. No immediate 5xx spike. Monitoring dashboards: token throughput stable, p95 latency increased +30% but within SLO.
jess (sre-lead): good. Runbook next steps: keep override for 2h, collect traces, engage infra to repro mem pressure, schedule model kernel/quant analysis if needed. If metrics degrade, rollback override and enable fallback.
beth (sales): telling Horizon: "We've applied a temporary pin to a higher-capacity safe model for your tenant and will monitor closely. This is to maintain response quality while we investigate source of the VPC pool instability. We'll update in 1h or sooner." :thumbsup:
cs-horizon: copied. They've asked for ETA for permanent mitigation; we should avoid promises. A short-term update in 1h is fine.
alex: infra says one GPU in their dedicated pool experienced kernel OOMs due to a bad compaction job. They've restarted the node; replication ongoing. INF-8712 updated.
maria: metrics look stable after 20m ramp. p50 down to baseline, error rate ~0.9%.
leo (oncall): handoff: I'm paged out at 1777778100 to evening oncall (maria). Handoff notes: override in place until 1777785122 (2h), canary ramp logged, infra ticket linked. Please monitor kernel OOM metric and KV-cache fullness.
maria: taking handoff. I'll schedule a follow-up with eng-runtime and infra for root cause and permanent routing tweaks.
cs-horizon: thanks team — I'll update Horizon with the note and file a post-incident request for a permanent tenant routing policy review.
incident-bot: Incident thread closed for paging but remains open for follow-up. Closure marker: mitigated by temporary pin & node restart. Follow-up required: INF-8712, RT-4457 (model routing review).
